Growth Mixture Models with Complex Survey Design

Source: R/gmm-survey.R
gmm_survey.Rd

Fits growth mixture models for longitudinal data with full integration of complex survey design features including stratification, clustering (PSUs), and probability weights. Implements the EM algorithm with sandwich standard errors for survey-adjusted inference.

Usage

gmm_survey(
  data,
  id,
  time,
  outcome,
  n_classes = 2,
  growth_model = "linear",
  strata = NULL,
  cluster = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  nest = TRUE,
  outcome_type = "continuous",
  fixed_variances = FALSE,
  fixed_timescores = TRUE,
  predictors = NULL,
  distal = NULL,
  auxiliary = NULL,
  starts = 500,
  convergence = 1e-06,
  max_iter = 1000,
  cores = 1,
  verbose = TRUE,
  keep_data = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Data frame in long format containing repeated measurements

id

Character string specifying the individual ID variable name

time

Character string specifying the time variable name

outcome

Character string specifying the outcome variable name

n_classes

Integer number of latent classes (default: 2)

growth_model

Character string specifying growth model type: "linear" (default), "quadratic", "nonlinear", or "free_basis"

strata

Character string specifying stratification variable (optional)

cluster

Character string specifying cluster/PSU variable (optional)

weights

Character string specifying sampling weights variable (optional)

nest

Logical indicating nested clustering (default: TRUE)

outcome_type

Character string: "continuous" (default), "count", "binary", or "ordinal"

fixed_variances

Logical, should residual variances be constrained equal across classes? (default: FALSE)

fixed_timescores

Logical, should time scores be equal across classes? (default: TRUE)

predictors

Character vector of time-varying predictor variable names (not yet implemented)

distal

Character vector of distal outcome variable names (use with r3step() function)

auxiliary

Character vector of auxiliary variable names for class membership prediction

starts

Integer number of random starts (default: 500)

convergence

Numeric convergence criterion (default: 1e-6)

max_iter

Integer maximum number of EM iterations (default: 1000)

cores

Integer number of CPU cores for parallel processing (default: 1)

verbose

Logical, print progress messages? (default: TRUE)

keep_data

Logical, store data in output object? (default: FALSE)

...

Additional arguments (reserved for future use)

Value

An S4 object of class SurveyMixr containing:

parameters

Class-specific growth parameters (means, variances)

class_proportions

Weighted and unweighted class proportions

posterior_probs

Posterior probabilities for each individual

standard_errors

Survey-adjusted standard errors

fit_indices

AIC, BIC, aBIC, entropy, log-likelihood

convergence_info

Convergence diagnostics from random starts

survey_design

Survey design information

Details

This function implements growth mixture modeling with full survey design integration, a feature combination not available in other R packages. The implementation uses:

  • EM algorithm with survey weight integration in the likelihood

  • Multiple random starts to avoid local maxima

  • Sandwich standard errors for stratification and clustering

  • FIML for missing data

The function automatically converts data from long to wide format internally for computational efficiency. Survey weights are normalized to sum to the sample size.

For model selection across different numbers of classes, see gmm_select. For analyzing auxiliary variables with classification uncertainty correction, see r3step.

References

Muthén, B. (2004). Latent variable analysis: Growth mixture modeling and related techniques for longitudinal data. In D. Kaplan (Ed.), Handbook of quantitative methodology for the social sciences (pp. 345-368). Sage Publications.

Asparouhov, T., & Muthén, B. (2014). Auxiliary variables in mixture modeling: Three-step approaches using Mplus. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 21(3), 329-341.

Lumley, T. (2010). Complex surveys: A guide to analysis using R. John Wiley & Sons.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load simulated data
data(mcs_simulated)

# Fit 3-class model with survey design
fit <- gmm_survey(
  data = mcs_simulated,
  id = "id",
  time = "age",
  outcome = "selfcontrol",
  n_classes = 3,
  growth_model = "linear",
  strata = "stratum",
  cluster = "psu",
  weights = "weight",
  starts = 500,
  cores = 4
)

# View results
summary(fit)
plot(fit, type = "trajectories")

# Check convergence
diagnose_convergence(fit)
} # }
